newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU DETAILS CONCERNS ABOUT KLM PRACTICES.
newsitem.headline: EU DETAILS CONCERNS ABOUT KLM PRACTICES.

text.p: The European Commission, acting on a complaint from cut-price British airline EasyJet over unfair practices, has issued a so-called statement of objections to KLM Dutch Airlines, a Commission official said on Thursday.
The document, which was sent on July 31, was the result of an investigation following EasyJet's complaint that KLM was trying to eliminate it from the London-Amsterdam route.

"So we have looked into it (the complaint)," the spokeswoman added. "And on the basis of what we have found have indeed sent out a statement of objections." She declined to give information about the document's content.
KLM was asked to give its side of the story. The next step should be a hearing on the case, but no date had yet been set.
"Nothing will happen before September," she said.
She was commenting on a report in Financial Times saying that the Commission will hold a hearing next month into allegations that KLM engaged in unfair practices against EasyJet.
In February, officials from the Commission visited KLM's head office and took away documents as part of its investigation.
KLM has said it has not done anything which is not in line with EU legislation.
EasyJet launched flights between Luton Airport, outside London, and Amsterdam in 1995, undercutting the prices charged by the Dutch carrier for flights between Amsterdam and London.
KLM responded by cutting its fares, prompting EasyJet to accuse the Dutch airline of predatory pricing and abusing its dominant market position.
